title: Methodology and Data Sources | Nomad Spin
description: How Nomad Spin city figures are built: which numbers are stored, which are formulas, which records are estimates, and how comparison and matching scores work.
h1: What our numbers are, and what they are not.
intro: You are deciding where to live. You should know how solid each figure is before you lean on it.
kinds.title: Three kinds of figure
kinds.intro: No figure on this site is a live measurement. Every number on a city page, a comparison or a match falls into one of the groups below.
kinds.editorial: Editorial records. {count} cities form the original set. Their monthly cost, internet speed, safety, climate and community scores were entered by the Nomad Spin editor. They carry no source link and no check date, so we call them editorial, not verified.
kinds.estimated.label: Estimated records
kinds.estimated.body: {estimated} of {total} city records were produced with AI assistance and have not been checked by hand. These cities are marked as estimates on their city page, in Compare and in Find Your Base, and Find Your Base can hide them.
kinds.formula.label: Formula values
kinds.formula.body: When a record has no figure of its own for a field, we work one out from another field with a fixed rule, and tag it. This applies to both kinds of record. The rules are listed below.
cost.title: What “monthly cost” means
cost.p1: Monthly cost is our estimate of what one person spends in a month in that city: rent, food, local transport and everyday costs. It leaves out flights, insurance and visa fees. We have not yet fixed one standard for the kind of housing it assumes.
cost.p2: In a spot check of 10 cities in November 2026, our figures were 35% to 67% lower than the ones on nomads.com. Read our number as a lean budget, and compare it with a second source before you commit.
formulas.title: The formulas
formulas.col.rule: Rule when no stored value exists
formulas.power.rule: From region: Europe, North America, Oceania = 9, Asia = 7, elsewhere = 6
formulas.note: Formula values are not observations. They cover most of the dataset: {longStay} of {total} cities for long-stay cost, {nightly} for nightly stay and {reliability} for connection reliability. Treat them as rough guides.
gaps.title: What we do not have yet
gaps.source: A source and a check date on each figure. Records do not store where a number came from or when it was checked. City pages show one date for the whole dataset, last changed on {date}. Treat every figure as a starting point, not a quote.
gaps.insurance: Health insurance cost is missing for {count} cities. Those show “No data”. We do not fill gaps with a guess.
gaps.neighborhood: Neighborhood-level data. Costs and safety are city-wide. The long-form guides cover neighborhoods for the cities that have one.
compare.title: How Compare works
compare.li1: A row names a leader only when one city is strictly best on a measure that has a clear direction.
compare.li2: Ties have no leader. Neither do preference rows such as temperature and nightlife.
compare.li3: Visa rows never have a leader, because the answer depends on your passport.
compare.li4: There is no overall winner. A missing figure stays missing and is counted as missing.
match.title: How Find Your Base scores a city
match.intro: Each criterion becomes a fit between 0% and 100%. The score is the weighted average of those fits. You set the weights; the starting mix below is a suggestion and has not been validated with users.
fit.budget: 100% at or under your budget. Falls in a straight line to 0% at {limit}% over.
fit.climate: 100% at your ideal temperature. Falls in a straight line to 0% at {tolerance}°C away. Uses the annual average.
fit.internet: 100% at or above your minimum speed. Below it, {cap}% of the share of your minimum the city reaches.
fit.safety: 100% at or above your minimum score. Below it, {cap}% of the share of your minimum the city reaches.
fit.community: The community score out of 10, as a percentage.
fit.visa: 100% when the common stay length covers the days you asked for. Below it, {cap}% of the share it covers.
match.flagged: A city that is over your budget or below one of your minimums is flagged on its card, and you can hide such cities with one switch. Equal scores are ordered by lower monthly cost. The scoring code reads only the city figures and your settings: booking and partner links have no input into any score or ranking.
visa.title: Visas, tax and safety
visa.body: Visa routes and stay lengths describe the common case and change often. Tax notes are general information, not advice for your situation. Check the official government source for your passport, and speak to a qualified adviser before you make a tax decision.
wrong.title: Found a wrong number?
wrong.body: Tell us which city and which figure, with a source if you have one, and we will correct the record. <link>Contact us</link>.
